signal.factor_name: Innovative efficiency based on patents granted scaled by R&D capital (EMI1)

economic_intuition.value: Firms that generate more patents per dollar of R&D investment are more innovatively efficient; investors may underreact to this less-salient information, producing higher subsequent returns.

source.quote: patents and patent citations per dollar of R&D
source.interpretation: The paper defines innovative efficiency as output per R&D input and motivates underreaction to this information.

definition.value: Patents granted in year y scaled by five-year cumulative R&D expenses ending in fiscal years y-2 through y-6 with 20% annual depreciation weights.

source.interpretation: The paper gives the Patents/RDC formula and describes the denominator as R&D capital.

calculation_steps: Use the patent grant date as the effective date and count patents granted to firm i in IE year y.
Set missing R&D to zero in computing the denominator, as stated by the paper.
Compute Patents/RDC as patents_y divided by R&D capital.
For June formation year t, rank firms using Patents/RDC measured in year t-1.

source.quote: two-year gap between R&D capital and patents
source.interpretation: The formula and lag structure are stated in the paper and linked to the patent application-grant lag.

sign.meaning: Higher Patents/RDC corresponds to the efficient leg; EMI1 is long high Patents/RDC and short low Patents/RDC.

source.interpretation: The factor name and formula establish the positive high-minus-low direction.

ambiguous_fields.details: The paper states missing R&D is set to zero when computing denominators, but does not state how to handle a zero total R&D denominator for ratio computation.
The paper says the NBER patent database includes Compustat-matched identifiers, but does not provide implementation-level merge keys.

The paper states size groups use the NYSE median size breakpoint; it states IE groups are based on the 33rd and 66th percentiles of IE but does not explicitly state whether those IE breakpoints are full-sample or conditional within size groups. The independent-sort wording implies independent IE breakpoints, but the exact breakpoint universe is not fully specified.

Set to null for the EMI factor because the paper states IE in year t-1 is fully observable at the end of year t-1 and forms portfolios at the end of June t for comparability. The explicit six-month lag sentence appears in the Fama-MacBeth controls subsection, not the Section 7 EMI construction.
